{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# Runway & shutdown cash notes
Leonard - started Sep 25, updated Sep 30

## Where we are
About two months before we have to let people go unless the bridge or an engine deal lands. Keep enough aside to close the company properly (legal, final payroll, state filings). No new commitments without the three of us agreeing.

## Shutdown reserve
Legal: ask our lawyer for a quote to wind down. Final payroll and accrued PTO through Gusto. Delaware franchise tax and the annual report are due in March whatever happens.

## Money still moving (for the cuts)
An account still has money moving if anything was spent, billed or paid out on it in September 2025, or a campaign on it is still switched on. Ad revenue paid to us counts (the warehouse has it by network and month). Spend or a charge the vendor has agreed in writing to drop doesn't count. Heads up on the warehouse: the spend tables have no Meta spend after April and no Unity cost at all, so for spend go by the receipts and whether the campaign is on. The finance ledger lumps the ad network payouts together under AppLovin/MAX and runs a month behind, so for what was paid to us use the ad revenue numbers by network, not the ledger.

## Cuts
Fred: marketing, UA and socials. Arthur: engineering, stores and data tools. I'll take software subscriptions and the card.

## Open
Bridge: still talking to two funds. Engine: NCsoft is slow, follow up next week.
", "id": "f_c612c0e68a27b3330eb46a", "name": "Runway & shutdown cash notes"}

### 1. **Ownership of Assets (Deliverables)**
   - **Risk**: The contract does not clearly state who owns the creative assets (videos, static ads, etc.) produced by [ORGANIZATION_NAME_0851]. This could potentially give [ORG_NAME_2505] ownership of the assets, which may limit Harmony Games’ ability to modify or reuse them freely without incurring additional fees.
   - **Recommendation**: Add a clause that explicitly states Harmony Games will own all intellectual property rights to the deliverables, allowing you to use, modify, or redistribute them without restriction or future costs. Here’s an example clause:
     - *“All creative deliverables, including video and static ads produced by Node Media, are the sole property of Harmony Games Inc., and Harmony Games shall have the right to use, modify, and distribute these deliverables as it sees fit, without any additional fees or restrictions.“*

### 2. **Payment for Additional Services**
   - **Risk**: The contract specifies that any resizing of ads beyond three standard formats will cost extra. While the contract says resizing outside the standard sizes is priced at $100 for videos and $30 for static ads, this could add up, especially if resizing becomes necessary across multiple platforms.
   - **Recommendation**: Consider negotiating either a cap on these additional fees or bundling more resizing options into the base fee, as resizing for different platforms may be a frequent requirement.

### 3. **Tax Implications**
   - **Risk**: The clause about taxes implies that Harmony Games is responsible for paying any applicable sales or use taxes on top of the agreed fee. Depending on your jurisdiction, this could increase your costs significantly if sales tax applies (e.g., Washington State has a 6.5% sales tax).
   - **Recommendation**: Clarify upfront whether the $5K monthly fee includes taxes or if taxes will be added. It may also be worth determining what specific taxes apply, as th[USERNAME_34353] could significantly increase your overall expenditure.

### 4. **Scope of Services and Changes**
   - **Risk**: The clause about “services outside the scope” mentions that any creative work not listed (like additional production) would incur additional fees. Without clear guidelines, scope creep could happen, leading to unexpected costs.
   - **Recommendation**: Define more clearly what constitutes out-of-scope work and ensure There is a process to mutually agree on fees for any additional work, perhaps via written approval from Harmony Games before the extra work begins.

### 5. **Termination Fees**
   - **Risk**: The contract allows either party to terminate the agreement with or without cause, but it specifies that if Harmony Games terminates without cause, you may still have to pay the full amount as if the services had been fully rendered.
   - **Recommendation**: Negotiate this clause to ensure that you only pay for services already rendered or prorated for the portion of the month. This will prevent you from being liable for the entire project cost if you choose to terminate early.

### 6. **Late Fees**
   - **Risk**: If Harmony Games does not pay invoices on time, There is a clause allowing [ORG_NAME_2505] to charge 1.25% interest per month on overdue payments. This could accumulate quickly, creating unnecessary financial strain.
   - **Recommendation**: Clarify that any disputes about invoices must be resolved before late fees are applied. You could also negotiate for a grace period before interest kicks in.

### 7. **Indemnification**

content.text:
The handover register is in the Company Ops folder, and I've replied to Leonard in your DM with what he asked for: how many are marked TRANSFER, and which outsiders still have access.

**The register** ([Marketing & UA Account Handover Register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UVXm264nKUSdKuea2GvIeKgw-dcX3V5wawZ4bvJ91i4/edit)) has one row for each of the 14 marketing, UA and social accounts in Arthur's Sep 30 sweep. Each row shows the company holders, the class, whether money's still moving, the action and the evidence. I shared it with Leonard and Arthur as editors.

| Action | Accounts |
|---|---|
| **TRANSFER (3)** | Instagram, X, YouTube |
| **REVOKE (3)** | Meta Domino Delights ad account, Unity Ads, TikTok @harmonygames |
| **KEEP (4)** | AppLovin, Google Ads 569-350-5790, LinkedIn, Discord |
| **CLOSE (4)** | Both AdMob accounts, adjoe, Google Ads 449-481-1590 (Calm Play) |

**Outside access:** Node Media LLC, the agency you brought in last year, still has admin on three accounts. On Meta it's a partner admin you shared in Oct 2024. On Unity Ads it's an advertiser admin. On TikTok @harmonygames it's Business Center admin, which wasn't in Arthur's sheet; TikTok sent you a reminder about it on Sep 18. I found no sign that any of it was ever removed.

**Calls you might want to know about:**
- **Instagram:** the only login is your personal Gmail, so under Arthur's rules it has no company holder. That makes it a TRANSFER.
- **Google Ads 569-350-5790:** the rules alone would close it, but Arthur emailed last night asking to KEEP it, in case a publisher takes Domino Delights and wants its history.
- **adjoe:** a campaign switched on by mistake in September, but adjoe agreed in writing on Sep 8 not to bill those installs. So it counts as no money moving.
- **AdMob:** September ad revenue was $39, under Leonard's $100 cutoff, so both accounts go to CLOSE.
- **AppLovin:** September ad revenue was $136, so it stays as KEEP.

**Done under Arthur's rules:** his card says socials marked TRANSFER go as a checklist on your "Lock up social handles and domain?" card on the UA/BD Trello board. I added a checklist there with Instagram, X and YouTube; each item is adding Leonard as owner.
